narrative.overview:
A workshop bench under good daylight, with labeled drawers and nothing hidden behind a cover plate. The visitor is a builder deciding whether runesm fits their product, and the fastest way to convince them is to hand them the tool and let them watch it work. Every surface is meant to be picked up and changed. Nothing is a display case.

The system takes its precision from Rams-era Braun product documentation: a machine explained without ornament, where every part is labeled in the same quiet voice and the labels are the design. It takes its warmth from paper rather than from decoration. The ground is a warm off-white, not white, and the ink is a warm near-black, not black.

Color here is information, never decoration. Four semantic hues communicate UI state, while a separate editor-only palette makes source structure visible without borrowing status meaning.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground, warm ink, warm neutrals: no pure white, no pure black, everything tinted toward hue 75
Four semantic UI hues with one job each, plus an editor-only syntax palette
Near-square corners (2-4px). Roundness is not a personality here
Flat by default. Depth comes from recessing what the machine writes into, not from shadows
Labeled panes as the organizing grammar, in the manner of equipment documentation
Motion is feedback only: it exists to make streaming legible, never to decorate

rules.name: The Four UI Jobs Rule
rules.body: There are exactly four semantic UI hues: rust for the brand and its links, sap for pass, crimson for fail, ochre for running. Syntax ink is confined to editor tokens and never carries UI state.

rules.name: The Ink Acts Rule
rules.body: The primary action is graphite fill with paper text, not a colored button. Weight, not hue, makes it primary.

rules.name: The Never Hue-Alone Rule
rules.body: Status is never carried by color alone. Removing all color from the interface must leave it fully readable.

rules.name: The Two-Ground Rule
rules.body: Only two background values appear in normal use: paper and paper-sunk. A third is a sign of a container that did not need to exist.

rules.name: The Labeled Drawer Rule
rules.body: Every pane carries a small uppercase Archivo label in graphite-soft. This is the deliberate organizing grammar, and the one place repeated uppercase tracked labels are correct.

rules.name: The Mono Is For Code Rule
rules.body: Martian Mono appears only where the content is code or machine output. Monospace as a costume for 'developer tool' is prohibited.

rules.name: The Sunk Well Rule
rules.body: Anything the machine writes into is recessed. Anything the user acts on is flush or raised.

rules.name: The No Ambient Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow on a resting element is prohibited. Use a ground change or a hairline instead.

dos: Do tint every neutral toward hue 75. Warm paper and warm ink, never #fff or #000.
Do keep the four UI hues to their four jobs and keep syntax ink inside editor source.
Do make the primary action graphite fill with paper text. Weight makes it primary, not color.
Do pair every status color with a text label, so the interface survives with all color removed.
Do recess surfaces the machine writes into, and keep surfaces the user acts on flush or raised.
Do use Martian Mono only for code and machine output. Everything else is Archivo.
Do vary spacing for rhythm across the 4/8/12/20/32/52 scale.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion on every transition.
Do give every control a visible 2px rust focus ring at 2px offset.
Do use rule-strong (3.39:1) for any boundary that identifies a control, and rule only for decorative hairlines.
donts: Don't use a border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe.
Don't reach for gradient mesh backgrounds, glassmorphism, floating 3D blobs, purple-to-pink palettes, or oversized rounded corners.
Don't add CRT glow, scanlines, blinking block cursors, ASCII art, or green-on-black.
Don't fall back to near-black plus one blue accent, uniform rounded cards, and a reflex-default sans.
Don't use background-clip: text with a gradient.
Don't wrap panes in bordered cards, and never nest a container inside a container.
Don't add a shadow to a resting element.
Don't introduce another UI hue, use syntax ink outside source code, or color a heading, icon, or panel chrome.
Don't set body text wider than 75ch.
Don't animate layout properties. Transition color, opacity, and transform only.
